image_transform: Whole views; aspect-preserving fit into common tiles, padding and identical labels. No flip or content crop.
cadence: All recorded frames retained; 10 control frames per playback second; display only.

notes.text: Open and align above the orange can for a gentle grasp and lift test; contents are not visually identifiable.
Descend with open fingers around the orange can, keeping the hand above its top.
Make gentle finger contact and begin a low lift, checking can retention rather than assuming the commanded aperture proves grasp.
The loose contact did not clearly lift the can. Close to a secure side contact and lift a short distance to test its response.
Test retention under a looser side contact during a small lift. Compare the other can if the response does not distinguish contents.
Hold over the original spot and reduce contact slightly to check for gravity-driven slip, without treating opening state as a force reading.
Continue the low-height contact test with a slightly wider opening, watching whether the orange can slips.
Orange slipped at wider contact and is back on the table. Move clear toward the blue can for the same lift comparison.
Align the open gripper above the blue can before lowering to comparable side contact.
Lower open fingers around the upper sides of the blue can, avoiding contact from above.
Establish light side contact on the blue can and start a short lift to compare its retention under a gentle grasp.
The blue can rose with the fingers. Continue the low lift while easing contact to compare gravity-driven slip with the orange can.
Ease to the same opening where the orange can slipped, keeping the blue can directly above its original position.
Both cans slipped when contact opened too far, so that test was inconclusive. Recenter on blue for a firmer, controlled acceleration test.
Settle a reproducible light side grasp on blue before lifting; opening is a position target, not a force measurement.
Apply a short vertical lift with light contact, then pause to observe inertial slip without moving the can over other objects.
Blue follows the light grasp without obvious slip. Test a marginally wider contact during a short upward pulse to help distinguish load response.
Blue remains securely coupled at 0.765. Set it back down before applying the identical light-contact lift to orange for comparison.
Release blue at its original table location and raise clear of both cans.
Return above orange at a safe height for a matching light-contact acceleration test.
Lower open fingers around orange to the same hand height used for the blue can test.
Establish the same light side contact on orange and allow it to settle before the matched lift.
Repeat the blue-can vertical pulse on orange with matching light contact and inspect for relative slip.
Orange also followed the first pulse. Match the slightly wider-contact pulse used on blue to check for a load-dependent difference.
Orange appears to have slipped relative to the fingers during the wider-contact pulse. Lower it back to the table before selecting the more stable blue can.
Release orange near the tabletop, then lift clear and move toward blue; the comparative slip favors blue but is not a direct weight reading.
Reposition the open gripper over blue at a clearance height, using the observed can location.
Descend around blue with the fingers open for a secure pickup.
Close on blue and initiate a gentle lift, checking that the can stays between the fingers.
Blue is visibly lifting with the gripper. Raise it above the neighboring can and basket rim before transporting.
Carry the retained blue can leftward toward the basket at rim-clearance height.
Continue carrying blue toward the basket while maintaining the secure grasp and clearance.
Center the retained blue can above the basket opening and slow to a stop before release.
Open the fingers while centered over the basket to release blue; verify its landing from the next views.
Keep the open hand clear while the released blue can settles inside the basket.
